about: The memory skill, the same in both SDKs (gap-closure plan item 2.1, 2026-09-26): the four tools the model sees,
what a `- memory: {...}` entry accepts, the namespace a verified caller's memory lives in, where the local tier
keeps it, the id an entry has in every tier, the token estimate and the compaction both agents run, and the
frozen notes both put in the prompt.
`namespaces` gives the caller in neutral terms, as tests/fixtures/sessions/sessions.json does (tier: owner, admin
or null; principals: what an access block verified, or null when none ran; user_id: a platform credential's
user), and each SDK builds its own auth from it.

function.name: memory_search
function.description: Search your memory: the notes you saved and the summaries of earlier conversations. Results come only from the memory of the caller you are talking to, the notes shared with every caller, and, when the caller is your owner, every namespace. Each result has key, namespace, description, content and updated_at.

query.description: What to look for, in a few words.

namespace.description: Owner only: search one namespace (owner, shared, or a caller namespace as memory_list names it).

limit.description: Most results to return (default 10, at most 50).

function.name: memory_read
function.description: Read one note in full, by the key your memory index gives it. Answers with key, namespace, description, content and updated_at.

namespace.description: Owner only: owner, shared, or a caller namespace as memory_list names it.

function.name: memory_write
function.description: Save a note to remember across conversations. key names the note (a short slug such as preferences or project-status: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores); writing an existing key replaces it. Give it a one-line description: that line is what your memory index shows in every conversation. The note is filed in the memory of the caller you are talking to. Only your owner may file under owner (the default in the owner's conversations) or shared (read by every caller).

key.description: The note's name, a slug such as preferences.

description.description: One line saying what the note is for, shown in your memory index. Without it, the note's first line is shown.

namespace.description: Owner only: owner (the default) or shared.

function.name: memory_forget
function.description: Delete a note by key from the memory of the caller you are talking to. Your owner may name the namespace to delete from. Answers with how many notes were removed.

namespace.description: Owner only: owner, shared, or a caller namespace as memory_list names it.

function.name: memory_list
function.description: List the notes in memory, most recently updated first: key, namespace, description and updated_at. Callers see their own notes and the shared ones; your owner sees every namespace.

limit.description: Most notes to return (default 50, at most 200).

namespaces.case: an admin is a caller like any other
the first identity an access block verified
a Portal Connect caller with no access block (principals unset, not the empty list)
an access block that verified nobody
a principal that is not a namespace (a comma, S-298) has none

entry_ids.about: uuid5 in the URL namespace over store, namespace and key joined by newlines, so an entry has one id in every tier and a sync merge by id is a merge by key.

keys.refused: memory: key must be a slug of letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores (up to 128), not "{key}".

tokens.about: ceil(characters / 4) over a message's text and its tool calls' names and arguments, plus 4 per message. The agent's compaction counts the same way (agents/core/context_compaction.py), which these cases run against since 2026-09-29.

transcript.about: How the older turns are given to the model that summarizes them.

notes.about: The memory index in the prompt (an index since 2026-09-29): sections in order, one line per note with its key and its description, or its first line without a heading's or a list's mark when it has none, cut to 120 characters; entries that do not fit the budget counted rather than shown. Nothing to show is no prompt at all.

namespace_grammar._comment: S-298 (2026-09-26): a namespace is owner, shared, or caller:<principal> with no whitespace and NO COMMA in the principal, in the SDK grammar (TS namespace.ts, PY memory_namespace.py) and on the portal (lib/storage/memory-scoped-service.ts). Lists travel as repeated `namespace` parameters, one value each; the comma-joined `namespaces=a,b` form is retired and refused. `probe` is the wave-2 review's case: a Web Bot Auth principal whose jwks path carries `x,owner`.
